0.long_answer: Salla disease, a type of free sialic acid storage disease, is caused by mutations in the SLC17A5 gene. This gene encodes for the lysosomal membrane protein known as sialin, which is responsible for transporting sialic acid out of the lysosomes. When sialin is defective, sialic acid accumulates inside the lysosomes, leading to the characteristic cellular buildup observed in affected individuals.
